sentences.text:
In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2026
 (Arising Out Of Slp (Criminal) No. 17715 Of 2025)
 Vipin Narwariya 
 Versus
 State Of Madhya Pradesh

O R D E R
1.
Leave granted.
2.  The appellant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.0483/2023 dated 02.09.2023 under Sections 498A, 304B and 34 of IPC registered at Police Station Hazira, District Gwalior.

As per the record,
the deceased-wife has unfortunately suffered an unnatural death within six months of her marriage,
i.e. on 04.08.2023.
The appellant-husband was consequently arrested on 24.09.2023 and has been in custody ever since.
Notably, other family members who were also arrested, have since been enlarged on bail.
3. At this juncture, learned State Counsel points out that seven vital witnesses have already been examined in the ongoing trial, though the Prosecution proposes to examine 34 some more time.

4. It is an admitted fact that the appellant has been in custody for more than 2 years at this point,
and in our considered opinion, his prolonged incarceration will serve no fruitful purpose.
5.

Accordingly, taking in consideration the period already spent in custody and the fact that conclusion of trial will take reasonable time, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, we allow the instant appeal.
The appellant is directed to be released on bail subject to the terms and conditions to be imposed by the Trial Court.

..........................CJI (SURYA KANT) ..........................J. (JOYMALYA BAGCHI) ..........................J.
(VIPUL M. PANCHOLI) NEW DELHI;
APRIL 02, 2026.
